candidates.source_name: CBCG — Statistika Platnog sistema Centralne banke Crne Gore (RTGS / DNS / IPS)
candidates.why_relevant: Core monthly and annual series for the central bank's own payment system: number and value of orders split RTGS vs DNS, system availability, and — since 20 July 2026 — the new IPS (instant payment) system volumes/values. This is the single most authoritative payments-volume series for Montenegro.
candidates.legal_status: official public statistics of a national statistics producer
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly scheduled HTML scrape of the page plus download of the attached monthly PDF indicators; parse order counts, values, RTGS/DNS/IPS shares into a time series.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language seed search then direct fetch of the CBCG page
queries_used: CBCG statistika platnog prometa broj i vrijednost transakcija
Crna Gora RTGS DNS sistem platnog prometa godišnji izvještaj CBCG

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Podaci o platnim uslugama i elektronskom novcu (quarterly PSP/e-money returns)
candidates.why_relevant: Quarterly ECB-style payments tables collected from all payment service providers and e-money issuers: users per payment service, cards issued in Montenegro, POS/acceptance devices, transactions per service type, card and e-money transactions, cross-border card transactions, transactions by terminal type, and cash deposit/withdrawal transactions. This is the card/ATM/POS and cash-usage backbone of the cell.
candidates.source_subtype: central bank statistical dataset (ZIP of data files)
candidates.access_status: public download (ZIP archives observed described on page)
candidates.legal_status: official statistics collected under the Odluka o izvještajima
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly crawl of the page, enumerate and download the ZIP attachments, unpack and normalise the tabular files into a per-quarter panel.
queries_used: CBCG statistika platnog prometa broj i vrijednost transakcija

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Statistički podaci: Platni promet section
candidates.why_relevant: Top-level statistics hub of CBCG; the payment-traffic branch sits alongside monetary, fiscal, external and capital-market statistics. Useful as the crawl root because deep payment-statistics URLs on this site change (a previously indexed /r/statistika/statisticki-podaci/platni-promet URL returned 404 on fetch).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use as crawl seed; re-resolve payment-traffic child URLs each run rather than hard-coding deep links.
queries_used: CBCG bilten statistički podaci platni promet publikacije "Zakon o platnom prometu" Crna Gora

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Kalendar objavljivanja statistike
candidates.why_relevant: Legally mandated advance release calendar (Law on Official Statistics) for the series CBCG is the official producer of, including payment traffic. Lets the collector schedule fetches on the exact publication dates instead of polling blindly.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Parse once per year plus monthly refresh; drive the scheduler for all CBCG payment series.
queries_used: CBCG "kalendar objavljivanja" statistike platni promet cbcg.me statistika saopštenja

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Bilten CBCG (monthly bulletin)
candidates.why_relevant: Monthly bulletin with a statistical annex covering monetary developments, the banking system, balance of payments and payment traffic. Gives a single machine-collectable file per month containing payment-traffic tables alongside context series, and provides a long back-run for time-series construction.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly download of the bulletin archive; extract the payment-traffic tables from the statistical annex.
queries_used: CBCG bilten statistički podaci platni promet publikacije "Zakon o platnom prometu" Crna Gora

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Izvještaj o radu CBCG (annual work report)
candidates.why_relevant: The CBCG states that the results of its payment-system oversight activity are published in the annual work report. That makes this the narrative and annual-aggregate counterpart to the monthly volume series — participants, incidents, availability, oversight assessments, project milestones such as SEPA and TIPS-clone.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual PDF download; text-extract the payment-system and oversight chapters.
queries_used: CBCG "nadzor platnih sistema" oversight izvještaj o radu godišnji Centralne banke Crne Gore platni sistem

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Nadgledanje platnih sistema (payment system oversight function)
candidates.why_relevant: Describes the oversight mandate, the systems under oversight and where oversight results are published; the natural pointer to designated systems, oversight standards applied and any dedicated oversight reports.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Low-frequency crawl for structural changes and new linked documents.
queries_used: CBCG "nadzor platnih sistema" oversight izvještaj o radu godišnji Centralne banke Crne Gore platni sistem

candidates.source_name: CBCG — RTGS sistem (system description page)
candidates.why_relevant: Defines the RTGS leg: gross real-time settlement between participants, the regulatory minimum transaction value that forces a payment into RTGS, operating hours and participant list. Needed to interpret the RTGS/DNS split correctly rather than mis-reading it as a retail/wholesale split.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Low-frequency snapshot for metadata/participant changes.

candidates.source_name: CBCG — DNS sistem (deferred net settlement description)
candidates.why_relevant: The retail/low-value leg of the national payment system — carries roughly 60% of order volume but under 6% of value. Essential for any retail-payments or cash-substitution analysis.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Low-frequency snapshot alongside the RTGS page.

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Podaci o realizovanom platnom prometu: RTGS i DNS sistem
candidates.why_relevant: The recurring monthly release of realised payment traffic (working days, total orders, total value, RTGS/DNS shares, daily averages). This is the page whose numbers are recycled by the Montenegrin press each month, so it is the upstream primary for those stories.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly scrape keyed to the statistics release calendar; parse the standard sentence pattern (radnih dana, broj naloga, vrijednost, procenat RTGS).

candidates.why_relevant: The secondary legislation that defines exactly which payment statistics must be reported, in which template and at what frequency (the Odluka o izvještajima koji se dostavljaju CBCG o platnom prometu, amended in Sl. list CG 82/17, 107/20, 10/26, 47/26 per search results). candidates.why_relevant: The definitive scheme-by-scheme list of adhering PSPs. Because Montenegro entered the SEPA geographical scope with an Operational Readiness Date of 5 October 2025, counting Montenegrin BICs appearing in the SCT, SCT Inst and SDD registers over time is the cleanest measurable proxy for SEPA migration depth — a series the CBCG does not publish as such.

negative_findings.description: The frequently indexed CBCG statistics URL https://www.cbcg.me/r/statistika/statisticki-podaci/platni-promet returned HTTP 404 on fetch, although it appears repeatedly in search results.
negative_findings.result_summary: Treated as moved, not dead. The CBCG site serves language/variant path prefixes (/me/, /en/, /r/, /c/, /e/) and appears to have reorganised the statistics tree; the live payment statistics live under /me/kljucne-funkcije/platni-promet/statistika-platnog-prometa/... Crawlers must re-resolve from the statistics index or sitemap rather than pinning deep URLs.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A collector pinning the old URL would silently lose the payment-traffic series and could wrongly record the source as dead.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated Montenegrin bank-association statistics publication was located. A local-language search for an Udruženje banaka Crne Gore card/ATM/POS statistics series returned only CBCG pages and individual bank sites.
negative_findings.result_summary: Either no such association series is published online, or it is not indexed under the terms used. Unlike Serbia or Croatia, Montenegro appears to have no bank-association-level payments statistics layer; CBCG is effectively the sole aggregator.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Removes a normally productive cross-check on card and terminal counts and concentrates single-source risk on CBCG.

negative_findings.description: No national card switch, domestic card scheme or local processor with published statistics was identified for Montenegro during this cell's searches.
negative_findings.result_summary: Assessment literature indicates ATM and POS routing and settlement run through international card scheme networks rather than a domestic switch, which is consistent with the absence of a national scheme statistics publisher.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Card-level transaction detail beyond the CBCG quarterly aggregates will have to come from international schemes or acquirer disclosures, not from a domestic switch — a structural gap for anyone modelling card economics in ME.

negative_findings.description: The quarterly payment-services and e-money dataset is described as distributed as ZIP archives; the individual archive URLs and their internal file formats were not enumerated in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Format and stable-URL pattern unverified. Not recorded as blocked — no access error was observed, only incomplete enumeration.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Parser design for the richest card/POS/cash dataset in the cell depends on the archive contents; this must be resolved before automation.

negative_findings.description: No open-data API, SDMX endpoint or bulk CSV service was found for CBCG payment statistics; the observed distribution channels are HTML pages, PDFs and ZIP attachments.
negative_findings.result_summary: Collection will be scrape-and-parse rather than API-based. Searches in both languages surfaced no data portal for CBCG.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Raises long-run maintenance cost and fragility of the payments feed, and makes the release calendar essential for scheduling.

negative_findings.description: The IPS (instant payment) system went live only on 20 July 2026, with a first-month figure of 56,678 transactions worth EUR 21.53 million.
negative_findings.result_summary: The instant-payments series exists but has almost no history, and it is unclear whether IPS will be reported as a permanent third column in the monthly release or only in ad hoc statements.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Instant-payment uptake is the highest-value forward-looking series in this cell but is not yet a stable, back-fillable time series; early monitoring of the release structure is needed to avoid a broken schema later.

negative_findings.description: No standalone annual payment-system oversight report was found; CBCG states oversight results are published inside the general annual work report.
negative_findings.result_summary: Oversight content is embedded rather than separately published, so it must be extracted from a large multi-topic PDF.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Oversight narrative (incidents, availability, designated systems) is harder to track and easier to miss than in jurisdictions with a dedicated oversight report.

coverage_gaps.description: The quarterly payment services / e-money ZIP dataset — the source of card, POS, terminal-type and cash deposit/withdrawal series — has not had its actual file inventory inspected.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch the page attachments directly, download one recent ZIP, inventory the contained tables and column headers, and record a stable field dictionary cross-referenced with the annexes to the Odluka o izvještajima.

coverage_gaps.description: No archive of past monthly payment-traffic releases was located; the CBCG page appears to present the current month plus an annual aggregate. Historical monthly RTGS/DNS values may only be reconstructible from Bilten back-issues or press reports.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test whether an archive index exists under the payment-traffic branch; if not, back-fill from Bilten CBCG monthly issues and use the Internet Archive for the release page as a fallback.

coverage_gaps.description: SEPA migration has no published national indicator. CBCG announces milestones but does not publish SCT/SCT Inst/SDD volume shares or the count of adhering Montenegrin PSPs.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Construct the indicator from the EPC scheme registers (count of ME-country adherents per scheme over time) and cross-check against CBCG press statements; flag it as a derived, not official, series.

coverage_gaps.description: Nearly all authoritative payment statistics for Montenegro originate from one publisher, CBCG, with no bank association, no domestic scheme, and no national statistics office series identified as an independent alternative.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Establish IMF FAS and the EPC registers as the only genuinely independent cross-checks, and treat local press only as a redundancy channel for the monthly figures.

coverage_gaps.description: MONSTAT (Statistical Office of Montenegro) and the Ministry of Finance were not directly scouted in this cell, although CBCG submits its release calendar to MONSTAT as part of the official statistics system.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout monstat.org and the Ministry of Finance for any payments or household-payment-behaviour series, and for the official statistics programme document that names CBCG's payment statistics obligations.

coverage_gaps.description: NASO (Nacionalna organizacija za podršku pridruživanju / National Adherence Support Organisation) surfaced only via trade press; its own web presence and any publications were not located in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search directly for NASO Crna Gora and determine whether it publishes an adherence list, a migration roadmap or progress reporting for SEPA scheme adherence.

coverage_gaps.description: Bilingual coverage was achieved (Montenegrin/Serbian plus English) but no searching was done in Albanian, spoken by a significant minority, and none in Italian or Russian despite the tourism-driven card-acquiring market.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a small Albanian-language probe for payment terms and consider tourism-sector acquiring commentary in other languages if card acceptance becomes a priority topic.

brief: Montenegro's payment-system statistics landscape is almost entirely centralised in the Central Bank of Montenegro (CBCG), which publishes a monthly RTGS/DNS realised-payment-traffic release, an annual aggregate, a quarterly ECB-style payment services and e-money dataset covering cards, POS terminals, terminal-type transactions and cash deposits/withdrawals, plus the Bilten monthly bulletin and the annual work report that carries the payment-system oversight narrative. Two structural events dominate the current picture: entry into the SEPA schemes' geographical scope with an operational readiness date of 5 October 2025, and the go-live of the national instant payment system (IPS, a TIPS-clone under an EPC licence) on 20 July 2026 with all eleven banks participating from day one — the latter creating a brand-new but very short instant-payments series. Distribution is scrape-only: HTML pages, PDFs and ZIP archives, with no API and a site whose deep URLs have already moved (one widely indexed statistics URL 404s), so collection must be driven off the statutory statistics release calendar and re-resolved from the statistics index each run. The main weaknesses of the cell are single-publisher concentration — no bank association, no domestic card scheme, no independent national aggregator was found — and the absence of any official SEPA-migration indicator, which is best proxied by counting Montenegrin adherents in the EPC scheme registers, with IMF FAS providing the only comparable independent ATM/POS density benchmark.
